label: Bible Study
prompt: _____ and built up in him, and stablished in the faith, as ye have been taught, abounding therein with thanksgiving.
verse: Rooted and built up in him, and stablished in the faith, as ye have been taught, abounding therein with thanksgiving.
note: Roots below, building above — Paul mixes a garden and a construction site.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Notwithstanding in this rejoice not, that the spirits are subject unto you; but rather rejoice, because your names are _____ in heaven.
verse: Notwithstanding in this rejoice not, that the spirits are subject unto you; but rather rejoice, because your names are written in heaven.
note: The seventy came back thrilled about their power; Jesus said rejoice in something better — your names in heaven.

label: Sunday School
prompt: Know ye not that they which run in a race run all, but one receiveth the _____? So run, that ye may obtain.
verse: Know ye not that they which run in a race run all, but one receiveth the prize? So run, that ye may obtain.
note: Paul borrows from the racetrack: everybody runs, but one gets the prize — so run like you mean it.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Then Peter said unto them, Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the _____ of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.
verse: Then Peter said unto them, Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.
note: Peter's answer to the Pentecost crowd's 'What shall we do?' — about three thousand responded that day.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: Speak ye _____ to Jerusalem, and cry unto her, that her warfare is accomplished, that her iniquity is pardoned: for she hath received of the LORD'S hand double for all her sins.
verse: Speak ye comfortably to Jerusalem, and cry unto her, that her warfare is accomplished, that her iniquity is pardoned: for she hath received of the LORD'S hand double for all her sins.
note: 'Speak ye comfortably to Jerusalem' — literally 'speak to the heart.' Handel's Messiah opens with these very lines.
